s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive vertigo with severe headaches and nausea, associated with a cerebellar mass
salient_findings: Severe bifrontal throbbing headaches with nausea and vomiting
Positive right-sided Dix-Hallpike maneuver with horizontal nystagmus
3 cm left cerebellar hemispheric mass with surrounding vasogenic edema
key_facts: 74-year-old man
History of metastatic prostate cancer
Known left upper lobe lung mass
Progressive vertigo for four weeks
Severe bifrontal throbbing headaches with nausea and vomiting
Positive for adenovirus
No focal motor or sensory deficits
Intact coordination on dysdiadochokinesia, finger-to-nose, and heel-to-shin testing
Intact gait despite dizziness
Positive right-sided Dix-Hallpike maneuver with horizontal nystagmus
Noncontrast head CT showed a 3 cm left cerebellar hemispheric mass
MRI of the brain demonstrated a cystic enhancing lesion in the left cerebellar hemisphere
Cerebral angiography revealed no abnormal hyperemia at the site of the lesion

shortlist.label: Cerebellar metastasis from prostate cancer
shortlist.why_kept: History of metastatic prostate cancer and presence of a cerebellar mass

shortlist.label: Hemangioblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic enhancing lesion in the left cerebellar hemisphere with mass effect

shortlist.label: Cerebellar infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Sudden onset of vertigo and headaches, with a cerebellar mass

shortlist.label: Cerebellar glioblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic enhancing lesion in the left cerebellar hemisphere with mass effect, although less likely given the patient's age and history

shortlist.label: Cerebellar astrocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic enhancing lesion in the left cerebellar hemisphere with mass effect, although less likely given the patient's age and history

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of metastatic prostate cancer and the presence of a cystic enhancing lesion in the left cerebellar hemisphere is consistent with a metastatic lesion, especially given the patient's known history of cancer.

rejected.label: Hemangioblastoma
rejected.why: While considered, the patient's history of metastatic cancer makes this less likely

rejected.label: Cerebellar infarction
rejected.why: The presence of a mass with surrounding vasogenic edema and a cystic enhancing lesion on MRI is not typical for infarction

rejected.label: Cerebellar glioblastoma
rejected.why: There is no indication of a primary brain tumor in the patient's history, and the imaging findings are more suggestive of a metastatic lesion

rejected.label: Cerebellar astrocytoma
rejected.why: Similar to glioblastoma, there is no indication of a primary brain tumor, and the patient's history of metastatic cancer makes this less likely
